884: One of the most central dogmas of neuroscience is that of functional localization:
885: the idea that specific cognitive and behavioral functions can be localized to specific
886: brain regions. This view has been updated to a richer, network-level view of behavior
887: and cognition. The history of human brain imaging is such that vast amounts of
888: natural language data have been generated in attempts to describe the populations
889: from whom brain images were recorded, under what experimental conditions, with
890: expert narratives describing the resulting brain maps. Together, these texts and images
891: provide a rich set of data upon which we collectively build novel hypotheses about the
892: neural basis of behavior, cognition, and disease.
893: Here, we introduce NeuroVLM, a generative AI framework that can serve as an
894: expert collaborator in this process of narrative building and hypothesis generation.

896: constrained to a finite, predefined corpus [3,11]. The text-to-brain model was expanded
897: to BERT-based text encoders [26]. More recent efforts have trained contrastive models
898: to rank similarity between text-brain pairs using LLM embeddings [16,17].

971: Looking ahead, we believe that it is critical to strengthen the ecosystem around
972: standardized benchmarks and reproducible evaluation. Network labeling and recall-
973: style retrieval provide accessible demonstrations, but they do not fully measure
974: neuroscientific correctness, robustness to analysis pipelines, or calibration under
975: dataset shift. Progress will benefit from community benchmarks that specify train-test
976: splits, map types, preprocessing, and query sets, and that evaluate multiple axes of
977: performance: retrieval utility, interpretability, out-of-distribution generalization, and
978: failure modes. Open model checkpoints, transparent preprocessing, and reproducible
980: NeuroVLM frames the neuroimaging literature as a bidirectional link between
981: how studies are described in language and where effects are reported in the brain.
982: This enables a single framework to support retrieval, labeling, and generation from
983: tens-of-thousands of tens of thousands ofpaired examples. These models can help orga-
984: nize a fragmented literature into a searchable, cross-modal interface: a way to move
985: from maps to candidate concepts and related papers, and from text queries to spa-
986: tial priors and exemplar results. By making these capabilities accessible with modular
987: components and modest compute, this work reduces the barrier to using modern multi-
988: modal methods for everyday neuroscientific workflows.NeuroVLM runs on a consumer
989: CPU, and the whole model retrains from scratch in about 1.8 hours on one GPU.

999: NeuroVLM is a step toward computational tools that augment, rather than replace,
1000: expert interpretation. Its most immediate value is as a literature navigation and
1001: hypothesis-generation aid that can surface relevant work, highlight commonalities
1002: across maps and descriptions, and provide interpretable suggestions. The broader
